requirement:
In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows source on the
same line MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
rationale:
**Verdict: not yet satisfied.** The shared implementation looks correct for Rust. The requirement says "in every supported language", and the tests and `{impl}` marking don't yet cover that.

**What is implemented and tested for Rust**
- `assign_comments` (`src/outline/mod.rs`) groups comments into runs. A comment joins the previous one only if neither trails code, only whitespace lies between them, the next comment starts on the line right after the previous one ends, and both have the same container-binding.
- Trailing comments form a run alone. `trailing_owner` gives them the innermost node covering the line, using the node line ranges as they were before comment widening.
- `run_owner` descends to the smallest node containing the run and picks the next child starting after it. When no child follows, the owner is that container, which is the root at top level. A container-bound run takes the smallest containing node.
- Rust binds inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container through `is_inner_doc_comment` (`src/outline/rust.rs`).
- `owner_at_line`, `comment_owners_at_line` and `nodes_for_lines` use the owners. `reference_selector` (`src/authoring/inputs.rs`) turns a reference into its owning outline node.
- The Rust unit tests in `src/outline/tests.rs` check these cases:
  - a run belongs to the next node;
  - a blank line splits runs;
  - a trailing comment forms its own run;
  - a comment in a body, or after the last item in a module, belongs to the container;
  - a top-level tail comment belongs to the root;
  - file-level `//!` and `/*! */` comments belong to the root.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs` has a search test for comment owners. `src/authoring/inputs.rs` has a test for the nodes that references contribute.

**Gaps**
1. **No ownership tests outside Rust.**
   - Every comment-ownership assertion uses `src/lib.rs`.
   - Python, TypeScript/TSX, CSS (including the `js_comment` kind), TOML and YAML have no test that their comments are recognised or assigned an owner.
   - Markdown HTML comments have only `assert_eq!(outline.comments.len(), 1)` in `markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading`. That test is marked `outlines`, not `outline_comments`, and checks no owner.
   - The language-specific parts are `is_comment` and `comment_binds_to_container` in each profile. The only language-specific part of ownership that is tested is Rust's inner-doc binding.
   - No test shows a Python `#` run, a YAML or TOML comment, or a Markdown comment following the "next node, else container" rule.
2. **Incomplete `{impl}` marking.**
   - Only `markdown::is_comment` and the Rust inner-doc function carry `outline_comments`.
   - The other comment-recognition code is marked only `outlines`: `rust::is_comment`, `css::is_comment`, `profile::kind_is_comment`, and each profile's `is_comment` / `comment_binds_to_container` wiring.
   - This code decides what counts as a comment, so it implements part of this requirement without an `{impl}` reference to it.
3. **Untested, ambiguous same-line case.**
   - `trails_code` treats any non-blank text before a comment on its line as source, including an earlier comment.
   - So `/* a */ /* b */` makes `b` a trailing comment by itself, although the text before it is only a comment.
   - The requirement doesn't say whether that counts as "source". No test pins the behaviour.

No `FIXME` or issue references acknowledge these gaps. Adding per-language ownership tests and marking the profile comment functions with `outline_comments` would likely let this pass.

:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file in the project. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When authoring evidence, the edges defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.targets` MUST determine the reference
contributions to the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`. The target of each edge leaving
the assessed subject MUST contribute; sources with only edges into the subject
MUST NOT contribute and remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. A `{cite}` made by the subject
contributes the cited definition's complete fenced declaration. An anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` contributes the complete anchored file.
An in-source `{impl}` or `{test}` reference to the subject contributes the source
containing it: for a reference in a supported language, the smallest enclosing
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; for a reference in a Markdown requirement, example, or
terminology declaration, that complete declaration; for other references, the
complete containing source file. Literal references, evidence copies, and
generated output MUST remain excluded under the existing reference-discovery
rules.
These contribution rules MUST apply only to edges directly leaving the assessed
subject. Including another declaration or source MUST NOT by itself recursively
expand that source's own edges. Reference links MUST NOT be described as proof
that all substantively relevant sources have been found.
